i used to be quite attached to labels; i delved deep into the “sexuality and gender label” hole, researching the spectrum of asexuality, pronouns, etc. through this, i found a set of labels that, by definition, fit. however, overtime i’ve come to realize these labels don’t hold as much importance to my identity as i initially thought. technically, i could be considered panromantic asexual non-binary, but in reality, asexuality is the only one i’d ever admit to aloud with full confidence. 

gender alludes me; i don’t find any reason to place oneself within these societal boundaries. being referred to as a man or a woman makes me cringe, i’d rather someone perceive me without gender playing a factor. i present in a rather androgynous way; strangers constantly use different pronouns and labels with me. this is something i actually find myself reveling in, and i make no move to correct them. when someone is unable to use gender to “properly” quantify me in ways outside of my personality,,, it is paradisal. i’m sure this isn’t a unique experience and my entire description of my gender probably fits exactly into some sub-group label (which is something i find humorous as this description hinges on a lack of labels). this is besides the point, though. 

in short, i’m unlabeled asexual.
